column1: # Format: odia <TAB> label <TAB> keys      labels: offensive, coarse, spoken, slang, dialect
# Whole words only, never substrings. The Odia cell must be canonical.
# keys (optional, comma-separated): the exact roman spellings under which the word may
# still appear in family mode. Choose keys NO innocent word shares: the lexicon also
# files words under loose casual keys, so the casual spelling is usually unsafe.
# Filter levels: off = nothing filtered; family (default) = offensive words only under
# their own keys, or when the user taught them; kids = offensive and coarse words never.
# See core/src/curation.ts. Phrases are not labelled: their offensive head word is.
# Inflected forms (with case or verb endings) are NOT covered until they are listed here
# Source: the owner's list, 2026-10-04. Keys were proposed by Claude from the measured
# collisions (see the commit message); rows marked REVIEW wait for the owner's check.
# Not "banda"/"band": those spell BANDA (closed). Not "gandi" below: GANDI (knot).
# Key "pella", not "pela": "pela" is the everyday spelling of PELA (push).
# REVIEW: also an ordinary word in Praharaj ("thickness; depth; hole"), 103 corpus uses.
#   Proposed coarse, not offensive: shown with a "can be rude" badge in family mode,
# REVIEW: Praharaj also gives "the bottom of a thing". Kept offensive as listed.
# Not in the lexicon; the rules spell it for chhodi (#2), chhori (#4) and chodi (#5).
# REVIEW: ordinary word first (curd), 360 corpus uses. Labelled slang (marked, not
#   filtered, also for kids) so the ordinary word is never hidden. Change to coarse to
# REVIEW: ordinary word first (hair), 1,473 corpus uses. Same reasoning as above.
